title: Support for local Snowflake OAuth
description:
Snowflake has a new auth type that targets desktop applications and could be a nice improvement over the `externalbrowser` hacks: [Snowflake OAuth for local applications](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/oauth-local-applications).

This is a regular OAuth authorization code flow with PKCE. The redirect URL must use `127.0.0.1` as a host and we can pass `LOCAL_APPLICATION` as the client ID (and secret, if using header-based auth). So it's desktop-only, the same as `externalbrowser`.

The authenticator for this is `OAUTH_AUTHORIZATION_CODE`.

It's possible that this means the `user` field is not required like it is for `externalbrowser`, which would be very nice.

title: Keypair auth does not use the shared session cache
description:
## Problem

Currently, `keypair_credentials()` has different behavior from other authenticators (`externalbrowser`, `workload_identity`):

| Auth Method | Uses `login_request`? | Uses Session Cache? |
|-------------|----------------------|---------------------|
| externalbrowser | Yes | Yes |
| workload_identity | Yes | Yes |
| **keypair (non-SPCS)** | **No** | **No** |
| keypair (SPCS) | No (uses `/oauth/token`) | **No** |

For non-SPCS cases, `keypair_credentials()` returns the JWT directly as a Bearer token with `X-Snowflake-Authorization-Token-Type: KEYPAIR_JWT`. This seems to work in most cases, but:

1. We regenerates the JWT on every call (~10ms overhead per my benchmarking last year).
2. No participation in the session and keychain caching.
3. We're inconsistent with other auth methods, which all go through `/login-request`.

## How the Python connector handles this

The [Python connector](https://github.com/snowflakedb/snowflake-connector-python/blob/main/src/snowflake/connector/auth/keypair.py#L188-L190) always goes through `/session/v1/login-request` for keypair auth:

```python
def update_body(self, body: dict[Any, Any]) -> None:
    body["data"]["AUTHENTICATOR"] = KEY_PAIR_AUTHENTICATOR  # "SNOWFLAKE_JWT"
    body["data"]["TOKEN"] = self._jwt_token
```

I can't find any evidence that they do the OAuth token exchange thing.

## Proposed fix

Refactor `keypair_credentials()` to match the session caching pattern used by `workload_identity_credentials()` and `externalbrowser_credentials()`.

We need to  investigate whether SPCS also accepts session tokens from `login_request` or whether this needs to remain a separate path.

title: Missing normalisation of account identifiers for keypair JWT generation
description:
## Problem

When generating JWT tokens for key-pair authentication, the issuer claim includes the account identifier. However, Snowflake account identifiers can come in various forms:

- `myaccount`
- `myaccount.us-east-1.aws`
- `myaccount.us-east-1.privatelink`
- `myorg-myaccount.global`

At present we use the account identifier as-is when constructing the JWT issuer claim. This can cause authentication failures for users with regional, PrivateLink, or "global" account formats.

A community contribution to `ellmer` fixed this specifically in the case of privatelink last year -- tidyverse/ellmer#694 -- but that change was never ported here.

The Snowflake Python connector normalizes the account identifier before constructing the JWT: https://github.com/snowflakedb/snowflake-connector-python/blob/d1251d9f01bbf06b4b58d09f81d5e0717cc546be/src/snowflake/connector/auth/keypair.py#L97-L100

```py
if ".global" in account:
    account = account.partition("-")[0]
else:
    account = account.partition(".")[0]
```

## Proposed fix

Adopt the Python connector's approach in `generate_jwt()`:

```r
account <- if (grepl(".global", account, fixed = TRUE)) {
  strsplit(account, "-", fixed = TRUE)[[1]][1]
} else {
  strsplit(account, ".", fixed = TRUE)[[1]][1]
}
```

This would ensure consistent behavior with the official Python connector across all account identifier formats.

title: Support for workload identity federation
description: Snowflake has released a new authenticator for [workload identity federation](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/workload-identity-federation) that could come in handy for some usecases. We should aim to support at least a subset of what it offers.

title: Misleading errors when `connections.toml` exists but does not have a `default` section
description:
I have a valid `connections.toml` but there's no `default` section. Instead of suggesting that I add one or pass another connection by name, I see something about the `account` parameter being required:

``` r
snowflakeauth::snowflake_connection()
#> Error in `snowflakeauth::snowflake_connection()`:
#> ! An `account` parameter is required when
#>   '/home/aaron/.config/snowflake/connections.toml' is missing or empty.
#> ℹ Pass `account` or define a [] section with an account field in
#>   '/home/aaron/.config/snowflake/connections.toml'.
```

<sup>Created on 2025-12-18 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

We should give more targeted errors in this case.

title: Misleading warnings when both `connections.toml` and `config.toml` exist
description:
When attempting to load a Snowflake configuration I see:

```r
> cfg <- snowflake_connection(name = "posit-software-pbc-dev")
! Both connections.toml and config.toml exist. Using connections.toml.
```

I do in fact have both files. However, I believe having both files is often valid. I suspect we're trying to guard against both files containing connections, but there are other settings in `config.toml` that we do respect (notably the default connection name).

I think the warning should only be emitted when connections are defined in both files, and the text of the warning should be

```r
> snowflake_connection(name = "posit-software-pbc-dev")
! Both connections.toml and config.toml define connections, but connections.toml takes precedence.
```

title: misleading error when connections.toml does not exist
description:
`snowflake_connection()` correctly indicates that the target connection does not exist, but the error implies that the connections file exists. It does not.

``` r
snowflakeauth::snowflake_connection("snowflake", .config_dir = "/tmp/does-not-exist")
#> Error in `snowflakeauth::snowflake_connection()`:
#> ! Unknown connection "snowflake".
#> ℹ Try defining a [snowflake] section in '/tmp/does-not-exist/connections.toml'
#>   or omit the `name` parameter to use the default connection instead.
```

Contrast this with the error that is produced when the connection name is not provided; the lack of a connections file is reported.

``` r
snowflakeauth::snowflake_connection(.config_dir = "/tmp/does-not-exist")
#> Error in `snowflakeauth::snowflake_connection()`:
#> ! An `account` parameter is required when
#>   '/tmp/does-not-exist/connections.toml' is missing or empty.
#> ℹ Pass `account` or define a [] section with an account field in
#>   '/tmp/does-not-exist/connections.toml'.
```

title: log more information about which configuration is being loaded and from where
support SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE
description:
https://github.com/posit-dev/snowflakeauth/blob/ecaeb7abe2ffdf3b6a08500ec94f65479027d366/R/config.R#L429

only `SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH` is included in the set of environment variables.

title: support private_key_file_pwd
description:
Support a private key with passphrase.

We have evidence of customers who declare both `private_key_file` and `private_key_file_pwd` in their `connections.toml`.

This may only require parsing the field and then providing the value to `openssl::read_key()`.

title: support private_key_path for backwards compatibility
description:
See: https://github.com/snowflakedb/snowflake-cli/issues/1480

Folks may be using `private_key_path` or `private_key_file`. This may depend upon how they originally configured their Snowflake connections file and what tools they were using at the time.

title: prompting for installation of jose blocks RStudio deployment
description:
When using push button deployment in RStudio, the prompt for `jose` installation appears in the R console, but the user is not able to interact with that while the deployment is open. The deployment window cannot be closed, and RStudio needs to be restarted.

https://github.com/posit-dev/snowflakeauth/blob/bb3e2a6c4e0afea5f7e34b9a70a2485f03b542d3/R/keypair.R#L37

Should suggested dependencies like `jose` become hard dependencies?

Workaround: Manually install `jose` before attempting push-button deployment.
